newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures up, March becomes benchmark.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures up, March becomes benchmark.

text.p: Three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures on TIFFE were boosted by a rise in Japanese government bond futures in the afternoon on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, the March contract took over the benchmark status, retroactive to Tuesday, as volume of the March exceeded that of the December contract for two days in a row.
The March contract's volume was 57,446 contracts, compared with 37,033 for December. The March contract moved in a range of between 99.05 and 99.10 in today's session.
The United States' second missile attack against Iraq, which took place during Tokyo morning, made a small dent in Euroyen futures prices, but its impact was quickly muted.

In the afternoon, a rise in Japanese government bond futures took up the futures contracts, but generally the market was considered range-bound. Dealers said it might be difficult for it to break out of its range before Friday, when U.S. payrolls data is due.
"We've found solid support around 99.00, but on the other hand, there were hard blocks at around 99.16/17 levels," said a dealer at a trust bank.

At the shortest end of the money market, the overnight rate inched up to 0.48 percent from Tuesday's 0.47 percent. A huge amount of tax payments resulted in tighter fund demand than usual, traders said.

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) money market operation was neutral, as has been usual for the past few weeks. The bank injected 300 billion yen into the market, which had a net fund shortfall of 310 billion yen before the operation.
In the open market, certificates of deposit (CD) rates were stable, with key three-month CDs issued at 0.53 percent. About 20 billion yen worth of issues were reported.
About 50 billion yen worth of one-month CDs and about 40 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were also issued at 0.53 percent.
All the rates were unchanged from Tuesday.
